names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 2 martie, «Sfântul Mucenic Nestor».
Read out of saint.gr's line for 2 Μαρτίου, «Άγιοι Νέστωρ και Τριβιμίος», with the rank word left off.

Read out of the title on the name link behind the line for 1 марта ст. ст., name page 6653, «Нестор Пергийский (Памфилийский), мч.», with the rank word left off. The line itself declines the name. Both epithets are part of the name the calendar’s index carries and both stay; the life page gives the region in prose and the day’s line gives neither. `.tmp/foldchk.py` reports no folder holding this form, and the bare «Нестор» is held by `nestor-of-maghid` as a Serbian form only.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 1 марта ст. ст. — «Мчч. Нестора и Тривимия (III).»

attestations.note: The Russian calendar keeps the pair one menologion day earlier than the Greek and the Romanian do: its line is on 1 марта ст. ст., where saint.gr and doxologia.ro both print them on the 2nd. The difference is one day and not the thirteen of the style conversion, so it is a difference between the calendars and not a conversion; the Sretensky life page for the two repeats its own day, «День памяти: 1 марта», and nothing read moves either reading onto the other’s day.

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 2 martie — «Sfântul Mucenic Nestor»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 2ης Μαρτίου — «Άγιοι Νέστωρ και Τριβιμίος»

attestations.note: One page holds him with Trivimios and puts them both at Perge of Pamphylia, in the country of the Kibyrrhaiotai, «κατά τους χρόνους του ασεβούς βασιλιά Δεκίου (249 - 251 μ.Χ.)». It closes with a hedge of its own: «Πολύ πιθανό, ο Άγιος Νέστορας, να είναι ο ίδιος με αυτόν της 28ης Φεβρουαρίου, διότι οι βιογραφίες τους συμπίπτουν» — very probably the holy Nestor is the same as the one of 28 February, because their biographies coincide. That is the site's own guess about an entry on another day and is recorded here without being acted on; the corpus keeps no Nestor on 28 February, and this row records the day page that was read. The page prints the distich «Ὁ τράχηλον Νέστορος πλήξας τῷ ξίφει, / Πληγὴν ὁμοίαν ἐντρίβει Τριβιμίῳ» and gives no relic and no hymn.
Not checked: the Ohrid Prologue at pravoslavno.rs for the corresponding Julian day (19 September 2026).

floruit.note: saint.gr: «κατάγονταν από την πόλη Πέργη της Παμφυλίας ... και έζησαν κατά τους χρόνους του ασεβούς βασιλιά Δεκίου (249 - 251 μ.Χ.)» — the reign is the page's own, given with those years. doxologia.ro, from which this folder was first written, gives him no year.
